- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 5 days, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–4% for 3–5 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day highs/lows to anchor forecast.
- Forecast horizon >30 days shows persistent lag: always adjust for 1–2% downward bias if true outcome is below 75% of forecasted mean.
